One clearing owner; six separate caches
+
Core owns reusable cache lifetime. TypeScript keeps the semantic algorithms.
direct trace
The TypeScript service holds one core scope and six typed handles. Clearing crosses the package boundary; the queries stay put.
REASON STATED
Independent key and value spaces are the PR’s reason for six handles instead of a shared map.

02
Cache entries keep their existing meaning
+
Preserve all six algorithms, key spaces, and promise/value identities. Treat undefined as a stored value.
direct trace
Five handles store promises by symbol identity. The sixth stores locations by file position; node arrays are rebuilt on access.
REASON STATED
The PR preserves existing query semantics and explicitly chooses Map.has because undefined is a valid value.

03
A rejected promise occupies a slot; a throw does not
+
Preserve semantic query failure behavior and promise identity.
direct trace
A returned promise stays cached after rejection. A synchronous factory throw leaves the slot empty. Old promises can settle after a clear without replacing new entries.
REASON STATED
The body makes preservation the constraint; the added characterization tests specify these two failure paths.

Release becomes an awaited boundary
+
Clear synchronously before project release. The PR explicitly adds an awaited backend release barrier.
scope needs
distinguishing
